title: Taskonomy: Disentangling Task Transfer Learning
abstract: arXiv:1804.08328v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Do visual tasks have a relationship, or are they unrelated? For instance, could having surface normals simplify estimating the depth of an image? Intuition answers these questions positively, implying existence of a structure among visual tasks. Knowing this structure has notable values; it is the concept underlying transfer learning and provides a principled way for identifying redundancies across tasks, e.g., to seamlessly reuse supervision among related tasks or solve many tasks in one system without piling up the complexity.   We proposes a fully computational approach for modeling the structure of space of visual tasks. This is done via finding (first and higher-order) transfer learning dependencies across a dictionary of twenty six 2D, 2.5D, 3D, and semantic tasks in a latent space. The product is a computational taxonomic map for task transfer learning. We study the consequences of this structure, e.g. nontrivial emerged

translated_abstract: 视觉任务之间是否存在关联，还是彼此独立？例如，拥有表面法线信息是否可以简化图像的深度估计？直觉对这些问题的回答是肯定的，这意味着视觉任务之间存在某种结构。了解这种结构具有重要价值：它是迁移学习的核心概念，并为识别任务间的冗余提供了有原则的方法，例如在相关任务之间无缝复用监督信息，或在单个系统中解决多个任务而不会累积复杂性。我们提出了一种完全计算化的方法来建模视觉任务空间的结构，这是通过在潜空间中寻找26个2D、2.5D、3D和语义任务之间的（一阶及高阶）迁移学习依赖关系来实现的。最终产物是一张用于任务迁移学习的计算分类图谱。我们研究了这种结构所带来的影响，例如非平凡的涌现现象。
tldr: 该论文提出一种完全计算化的方法，通过发现26个视觉任务之间的迁移学习依赖关系，构建了首个任务迁移学习的计算分类图谱（Taskonomy），揭示了视觉任务空间的内在结构。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a fully computational approach that models the structure of visual task space by discovering transfer learning dependencies among 26 vision tasks, producing a computational taxonomic map (Taskonomy) for task transfer learning.
